primary_sources.title: Vassilevich, Heat kernel expansion: user's manual
primary_sources.reviewed: The general mixed boundary coefficient (5.33), including tangential derivatives and derivatives of the smearing function, and the local conformal variation in section 7.1, equations (7.4)-(7.8). These passages were opened directly.
primary_sources.use: Derivative weights and locality justify the fixed-frequency endpoint power count. The actual paired Dirac domain and all finite-cut conversion fluxes come from the retained domain-specific derivation, not an independently chosen bag boundary condition.

source_access: The primary review and the relevant formulas were opened directly. No downloaded-byte digest is claimed.
strongest_comparators: The existing stationary action is differentiable on a faster phase excluding these traces. The preceding symplectic calculation makes one phase relation necessary for a maximal separated reflecting domain, but does not establish action convergence on that domain. Generic scalar limit-cycle theory does not evaluate the retained gravitational GHY, Weyl boundary action and covariant loop counterterms.
hardest_step: Keep the literal bulk/boundary pair, the vacuum cosmological shift and volume-counterterm variation together. Evaluate the complete cutoff term before removing the regulator. Distinguish a simple linear logarithmic conformal path from a nonlinear boundary phase, because an r^-3 second-order tail changes the same finite quadratic term.
new_consequence: The uncompleted static fast conformal path has a divergent linear action term; a nonzero thermal harmonic still has a nonconstant quadratic cutoff oscillation for every phase. A concrete periodic second-order tail equation can cancel that oscillatory action value, but matching it to the full variational and field equations remains open.
regulator_contract: Fixed background canonical cut; no unproved identification with a field-dependent fixed-physical-area cut. Relative canonical determinants cancel at the identical cut along the conformal path.
verification_scope: Exact original nonlinear densities and boundary-path conversions; charged static annular integrals at two precisions; independent complex-amplitude Taylor extraction; algebraic second-order-tail controls. The nonzero-frequency endpoint extension is an ordinary local power-count proof, not a numerical full dynamic boundary-action calculation.
